subject: Regional custody mapping & emergency routing for PrivateStack (EU/APAC) - action items
messages:
From: Paul Thomas <paul.thomas@anzubank.com>

Cc: AnzuBank Legal <contracts@anzubank.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Mar 2025 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Custody mapping & emergency routing questions for PrivateStack (EU/APAC)

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the intro call today. We're evaluating Redwood's Private deployment for a multi-country footprint and have a handful of concrete questions that will impact our control and audit plan:

- Can Redwood bind KMS per-tenant in a cross-region private topology? We require sovereign KMS for EU tenants, APAC tenants may use our regional KMS.
- In an outage scenario, do you support automatic read-only failover to a warm region (e.g., EU primary, APAC warm) while preserving residency proof for audit?
- What telemetry/audit artifacts do you produce for data custody handoffs (signed timestamps, control-plane logs, and egress proof)?
- We need a short matrix that maps where ephemeral caches, backups, and logs are stored by default.

I've attached our questionnaire (AnzuRegReq-questions.xlsx) with the above broken out. Can your team provide a draft mapping and a short runbook for emergency cross-region routing?

We'd like to schedule a technical alignment next week (preferably Tue/Wed) with your infra lead and our platform security.

Regards,
Paul Thomas
Head of Platform Security
AnzuBank

Attachment: AnzuRegReq-questions.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Custody mapping & emergency routing questions for PrivateStack (EU/APAC)

Paul — thanks for the clear list and for sending the questionnaire. Looping in Marissa (solutions), Vivek (product/ops), and Soojin (security) to draft the mapping and runbook.

Quick notes / proposed approach:

- KMS: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS per deployment. For multi-region PrivateStack we can bind KMS to tenant-region pairings (requires KMS endpoints in each region). We'll document required IAM/KMS policies.
- Failover model: we recommend an "explicit custody handoff" pattern: EU remains primary for EU-scoped tenants; APAC is a warm standby that can be promoted to read-only under controlled procedures. Automatic promotion is possible but we advise canary gating to preserve compliance evidence.
- Telemetry: control-plane audit logs, signed cluster timestamps (RFC3339), and per-request source-region metadata are emitted. We'll include sampling guidance for full egress proof.
- Caches/backups/logs: default placement varies by deployment profile; I'll attach a starter matrix and topology sketch.

Next steps:
1) Marissa will assemble a custody mapping table and a suggested runbook.
2) Vivek to confirm SLA implications for warm promotions and any quota impacts.
3) Soojin will add minimum evidence items (log retention, signed timestamps, KMS proof).

We have availability Tue 18 Mar 09:00–12:00 UTC and Wed 19 Mar 14:00–17:00 UTC. Which works for your infra/security folks?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: privatestack-region-matrix-draft.pdf (PDF, 120KB), topology-sketch.v1.png (image, 220KB)

Folks — quick draft notes inline and an attachment with the custody matrix. Quoted above for context.

> Paul — thanks for the clear list and for sending the questionnaire. Looping in Marissa...

Proposed draft (high level):

1) Tenant-region binding
- Each tenant record is pinned to a primary region in the control plane (EU or APAC). The data plane nodes for that tenant are instantiated in the associated VPCs.
- KMS: we support per-tenant key aliasing. For EU tenants we require customer-managed keys in an EU KMS; we will not cache plaintext keys outside the region.

2) Failover choreography (emergency routing)
- Normal: EU primary serves traffic from EU DNS and load balancers (regional egress).
- Incident: runbook step 1 = execute custody snapshot (signed cluster timestamp + control-plane audit bundle); step 2 = update routing policy to direct read-only traffic to APAC warm nodes; step 3 = observe canary traffic for 15 minutes, collect signed request logs.
- The warm region will be configured with KV cache warm-up and pre-fetching of tenant KV state; we keep a rolling 24–72 hour replay window depending on customer SLAs.

3) Audit artifacts (minimum deliverables)
- Control-plane audit bundle (GZIP) with signed timestamps and request-origin headers.
- KMS envelope metadata per snapshot (key id, region, signature).
- Network egress records with ASN-level routing metadata.

4) Backups & transient data map
- Backups: encrypted incremental snapshots are stored in region by default; cross-region replication only after customer opt-in.
- Ephemeral caches: TTL-limited, region-local by default; can be configured to replicate to warm nodes for faster failover (customer choice).

Open questions for APAC runbook (Paul / Anzu to confirm):
- Does Anzu want automatic promotion of APAC to read-write in certain emergency classes?
- Retention window for signed custody artifacts (we recommend 90 days minimum for financial audits).

I attached the custody-mapping-table.csv with columns: tenant_id, primary_region, kms_alias, backup_policy, cache_replication. We'll convert to a shared Drive link after Anzu confirms.

Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachment: custody-mapping-table.csv (CSV, 18KB)
